title: Split routes.py into focused modules
desc: The triplicated way-resolution pipeline has been consolidated into a shared _resolve_way helper, but routes.py is still ~1,900 lines mixing annotations, way editing, planning, and wormhole sharing in one blueprint. Splitting it into per-concern modules (annotations, way edits, planning, sharing) would improve navigability.

title: Speed up planning hot paths with native extensions
desc: The main bottlenecks are the Python _bresenham generator and _segment_cost in RRT* (called O(max_iter × neighbors) times), and the heapq loop in grid_astar. Recommended approach: (1) try @numba.njit on these inner loops first — zero build overhead, easy to toggle; (2) replace grid_astar with skimage.graph.route_through_array which is C-backed; (3) Cython or pybind11 only if numba is unacceptable for deployment. Full C/C++ rewrite is not justified given that numpy, cKDTree, and Shapely/GEOS are already native.

title: Elevation-aware planning costs
desc: Integrate DEM tiles and add a slope penalty term in PathGrid.fill so the planners avoid steep terrain, not just tagged obstacles.

title: Viewer undo/redo built on the existing change_log
desc: The annotation store already records ordered, timestamped change entries; exposing undo/redo in the UI would mostly be frontend work plus inverse operations for each change type.

title: Progress reporting for fetch_area via SocketIO
desc: The fetch task is polled over REST while a SocketIO channel already exists for telemetry — pushing progress (query, parse, save stages) would remove the polling and its 404-on-second-poll footgun.

title: cost_grid and replan accept unbounded/unvalidated client parameters
desc: get_cost_grid deep-copies the merged map and fills a 1 m grid over any client-supplied bbox with no area cap (unlike fetch_area's MAX_FETCH_AREA_KM2), then reprojects every cell in a Python loop — a compute/memory DoS lever. create_replan passes client JSON (cell_size, cost dicts) into the planner without type/range validation. Fix: clamp bbox area/cell count and validate parameter types up front.

title: Multipolygon inner rings are never subtracted
desc: parse_osm_rels only labels inner member ways with in_out="inner" (used for display); nothing cuts them out of the outer polygon. A courtyard inside a building relation or an island in a lake is covered by the outer barrier polygon and planned around as untraversable. Fix: build outer rings as Polygons with holes in parse_osm_rels/combine_ways.

title: combine_ways leaves merged members in ways_dict — duplicate classification
desc: The merged negative-id way is added but the original relation members stay in ways, so separate_ways classifies both. Any member carrying its own classifying tags (e.g. waterway=riverbank ways in a water relation) yields duplicated barrier geometry and doubled point clouds. Fix: drop or mark consumed member ids after a successful merge.

title: info.py total footway distance sums buffer perimeters
desc: By the time footways are saved they have been through buffer_line and are Polygons, so w.line.length is the buffer perimeter — the reported stat is roughly 2× the real path length plus the cap arcs. Fix: derive length from node coordinates (or keep the centerline). get_stats has no tests, which is how this survived.

title: Degenerate OSM ways abort the entire parse
desc: A way with one node makes LineString raise, and a closed 3-node way [a, b, a] sets is_area=True and Polygon raises ("linearring requires at least 4 coordinates"). One malformed way in a response or hand-edited cache kills run_parse with an unhandled exception. Fix: skip-and-warn ways with too few distinct coordinates.

title: Non-atomic .mapdata/cache writes can destroy the previous good file
desc: save_mapdata and the OSM cache writer open the target with "w" and json.dump directly; a crash, Ctrl-C, or full disk mid-dump leaves a truncated file where a valid one was (and create_mapdata without -d re-saves over the file it just loaded). Fix: write to a temp file in the same directory and os.replace.

title: Path simplification runs after collision checking and can chord into obstacles
desc: In replan smoothing is collision-checked but the subsequent LineString(path).simplify(cell_size) (tolerance equal to the default obstacle inflation) is not, so a path hugging an inflated obstacle can be chorded into it; grid_astar's internal simplify has the same gap. RRT*'s _simplify_path checks every shortcut and is the model to follow. Fix: collision-check the simplified result and fall back, or simplify before smoothing.

title: RRT* rewiring leaves stale costs and a stale informed ellipse
desc: After parent[idx] = new_idx the cached costs of the rewired node's descendants are never updated, so later parent-selection/rewiring comparisons use wrong values and cost[goal_idx] can misreport the path cost. Separately, goal rewires through the generic loop bypass _best_cost, so informed sampling keeps a larger-than-necessary ellipse. Paths stay collision-free but suboptimal. Fix: recompute cost via parent-chain traversal (or update children on rewire) and sync _best_cost with cost.get(goal_idx) each iteration.

title: Three viewer endpoints 500 on missing JSON content type
desc: cancel_replan_route, create_wormhole, and cancel_wormhole call request.json.get(...); a request without Content-Type: application/json or with an empty body yields an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 400. Fix: (request.get_json(silent=True) or {}).get(...) as the other handlers do.

title: Fetch-task and cancelled-transfer registries grow without bound
desc: _fetch_tasks entries are pruned only when a client re-polls the same task 60 s after completion — abandoned tasks accumulate forever. ReplanPath's cancelled-transfer set keeps IDs whose cancel arrived after replan() returned, and a reused transfer_id is then instantly "cancelled". Fix: sweep terminal tasks on each fetch_area POST and discard cancel IDs in a finally at replan entry/exit.

title: GraphPlanner.plan() edge cases: empty-array return and unlimited waypoint snapping
desc: With fewer than two waypoints the loop never runs and a (0,) np.array([]) is returned — neither the documented "(M, 2) array or None" contract nor checkable as failure. Separately, _find_closest_edge snaps waypoints to the globally nearest edge with no distance cap, so a waypoint clicked 500 m off the network silently produces a huge straight connector (annotation splicing uses an explicit 5 m threshold). Fix: guard the waypoint count and add a configurable max snap distance.

title: Grid cells are sampled at their lower-left corner, not their center
desc: fill, burn_obstacles, and grid_astar's back-conversion all use low + i*cs, so obstacle membership is decided half a cell off-center: a sub-cell obstacle straddling no corner sample burns nothing, and burned regions shift ~cs/2 toward −x/−y. Mostly masked by inflate_obstacles. Fix: add cs/2 in the three places plus test updates.

title: Latent input-shape traps in MapData helpers
desc: A 1-D (2,) current_robot_position (or a 2-column position against 3-column elevation waypoints) raises a cryptic np.concatenate error; _csv_to_dict on a single-row CSV iterates characters because np.genfromtxt returns 1-D; a loaded MapData lacks the points attribute that constructed instances have. Fix: np.atleast_2d + column checks, and restore points on load.

title: Version the .mapdata format
desc: The JSON schema has no format_version field, so future changes cannot be detected or migrated, and way_from_dict hard-KeyErrors on files missing newer keys (the crossroads list already needed a .get band-aid). Fix: write a version marker and use .get defaults on load.

title: Injectable RNG for RRT*
desc: All sampling draws from the module-global random: planning failures from the viewer cannot be reproduced, concurrent Flask request threads interleave draws non-deterministically, and tests must hack the global seed. Fix: accept rng: random.Random | None in __init__ and thread it through.

title: Vectorize Way.to_pcd_points and smooth_path hot loops
desc: The polygon branch materializes a MultiPoint over the full bbox grid and filters point-by-point with prepared.contains (~1M Point objects for a 500×500 m barrier at density 2) — shapely.contains_xy does this vectorized with no object churn; the segment loop grows pcd_points with np.concatenate per segment (quadratic copying). smooth_path is a scalar triple-loop that vectorizes directly as a Jacobi iteration. Distinct from the backlogged native-extension item (which covers the RRT*/grid_astar raster loops).

title: Cache /api/mapdata responses
desc: Every call shallow-copies the cached map, re-applies all edits (recomputing crossroads_list via parse_intersections whenever any edit exists), and rebuilds the full GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Fix: cache the merged GeoJSON keyed on (mapdata mtime, annotation-store hash), or serve an ETag and honor If-None-Match.

title: Pin ruff to one version across CI, pre-commit, and dev extras
desc: CI installs unpinned latest ruff while pre-commit pins v0.11.13 — this drift already caused the ruff-0.16 reformat churn commits. Pin the [dev] extra and CI to the pre-commit rev (or bump all three together).

title: CI tightening: strict docs build, demo smoke on PRs, enforced coverage
desc: mkdocs build lacks --strict, so broken links deploy silently; the viewer demo smoke test runs only on push to master, discovering breakage post-merge; coverage is measured but has no --cov-fail-under and is never published; ci.yml lacks workflow_dispatch. All small YAML changes.

title: Delete dead code and misleading names in the geometry/planner helpers
desc: points_to_graph_points and increase_line have no callers (and the offset-row distance metric adds parallel and perpendicular components linearly — wrong if ever revived); RRT*'s _is_collision segment branch is unreachable; GOAL_SAMPLE_BIAS doubles as the unrelated traversable-cell sampling bias; the density parameter across geometry helpers actually means spacing (callers pass 1/density).

title: Route all viewer filename handling through one validated resolver
desc: GET endpoints call _safe_data_path but many mutating endpoints pass the raw filename straight to _annotation_path, which contains traversal only incidentally (via Path.stem) and never verifies the referenced .mapdata exists. Harmless today but inconsistent defense-in-depth. Related lifecycle nit: create_app has no idempotency guard — a second call double-starts the telemetry thread and re-inits the ROS node.

title: Repo hygiene batch
desc: Delete the stale todo_fixes_plan.md at the repo root (PR #12 merged, its fixes verified landed); drop the unused python3-joblib from package.xml; add .mypy_cache/ to .gitignore; consider a CI check asserting the version triplicated across pyproject.toml/package.xml/CITATION.cff stays in sync.

title: Cheap linter/typechecker wins
desc: mypy: add check_untyped_defs, warn_unused_ignores, warn_redundant_casts (none require stubs). ruff: add the RUF, C4, and PT rule families (PT is valuable given the ~3,000-line test suite).

title: Wire up or remove the node anti-tag mechanism
desc: parameters/anti_obstacle_tags.csv is loaded nowhere and parse_osm_nodes has no anti-tag override analogous to Way.is_barrier. Related: way_node_ids is built from all ways, so obstacle nodes sitting on any way (the normal OSM position for barrier=gate/bollard) are always skipped and never become obstacles — if intentional, document it.

title: Cover the riskiest viewer endpoints
desc: No tests exist for the MAP_DATA_ACCESS_TOKEN gate (on/off), virtual-ID suffix validation in delete_way/restore_way, get_cost_grid, create_replan, upload_mapdata, add_way_node, or the wormhole endpoints. The auth and virtual-ID tests are the highest value.

title: Cover get_stats, combine_ways edge branches, and grid_astar cost behavior
desc: info.get_stats is untested (the perimeter-vs-length bug survived because of it); combine_ways' backward-prepend and ring-closing merge branches are untested; nothing asserts grid_astar actually prefers low-cost corridors (grid_cost_weight never exercised) or checks diagonal corner-cutting; the replan cancellation machinery is untested.

title: Centralize pytest config and the Overpass mock fixture
desc: There is no [tool.pytest.ini_options] and no tests/conftest.py: coverage flags live only in the CI workflow (local runs differ from CI), and the mocked-Overpass setup is duplicated across test_integration.py and test_viewer_routes.py. Add addopts and a shared fixture.
